subject: Energy
title: Hydrogen as Energy Storage
description: One-minute skill: Hydrogen as Energy Storage.

hook.text: Hydrogen stores energy chemically—produced by splitting water with electricity, then burned or used in fuel cells.

buildup.text: Electrolyzers split H₂O into H₂ and O₂ using renewable electricity—the hydrogen can be stored and transported.

discovery.text: Hydrogen can be stored in salt caverns for months—making it ideal for seasonal storage that batteries can't handle.

twist.text: Round-trip efficiency is only 25–35%—much energy is lost in electrolysis, compression, and conversion back.

climax.text: Despite low efficiency, hydrogen may be the only viable option for storing weeks of renewable energy at scale.

punchline.text: Inefficient but unmatched for scale—hydrogen stores seasons.
